chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from some of our companions, who said:

I was present with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), Harun al-Khalifah, Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya in Medina. They came to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Harun stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood aside.
Then Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Isa stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood with Harun.
Then Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan, 'Step forward,' but he refused. So Ja'far stepped forward, offered greetings, and stood with Harun.

Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) stepped forward and said, 'Peace be upon you, O my father. I ask Allah, who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided [people] through you, to send blessings upon you.'
Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he say what I heard?' Isa said, 'Yes.' Harun said, 'I bear witness that he is truly his father.'
ai.seo_question: What happened when Imam Musa al-Kadhim visited the Prophet's grave with Harun al-Khalifah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the theological distinction between political authority and spiritual lineage, as Harun al-Rashid witnesses Imam Musa al-Kadhim’s superior greeting to the Prophet. The Imam’s specific invocation of divine selection (*istifa*) and guidance (*hidaya*) underscores the Shia concept of *ismah* and the Prophet’s unique status, prompting the Caliph to affirm the Imam’s true paternity. This narrative serves as a key evidence for the Imam’s direct connection to the Prophet’s spiritual and biological lineage.
